findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a user has an older Codex installed with OpenAI's standalone installer.
OpenAI's [0.125 installer](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.125.0/scripts/install/install.sh) creates the standalone layout this branch recognizes, but the [0.125 CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.125.0/codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs) has no `update` subcommand. Forge therefore starts its interactive CLI with `update` as a prompt; because `repo.run` pipes stdin (`src/forge/repo.py:252`), it fails instead of updating. The recovery line repeats `codex update`, so it cannot perform the update either. The test stub at `tests/test_upgrade_updates_agent_tools.py:26` gives its old CLI an update command and misses this case.
findings.title: Functional: Recognize the supported standalone and Windows npm installations

stop.reason: Owner chose one more small round: run codex update only when that Codex has the command, else print OpenAI's install line

why: After a Forge upgrade, Claude Code and the Codex CLI on the machine stay on old versions, because nothing updates them.
